title: bug: DELIVERY_RECEIPT_CONFLICT deletes a strong receipt journal before finalize_attempt, so a lost finalize strands the attempt in finalizing with nothing to replay
description: receipt_send's conflict branch (scripts/moe-agent.sh, `rm -f "$journal"` after the DELIVERY_RECEIPT_CONFLICT warn) and its twin Send-MoeReceipt (moe-agent.ps1, $keep only when the RPC said ok) remove even a verified-local journal before finalize_attempt runs. This breaks CQ-V08b, under which a strong journal goes only once its attempt is closed. If that finalize then gets no answer (live landing or pre-flight replay, shared or worktree mode), the attempt stays finalizing, qa_approve and every claim of the task stay held, and no journal is left for the next replay to finalize. Repro: FAKE_EVIDENCE_MODE combining receipt-conflict with finalize-loss. Found by task-527735ea's self-review (it mirrors shared mode as its DoD requires, so it did not change this).

implementationPlan.description:
Fix, in both wrappers: a DELIVERY_RECEIPT_CONFLICT keeps a strong receipt journal until its attempt is closed (CQ-V08b).
Today (d35f2bc3):
- sh receipt_send (scripts/moe-agent.sh, about :6464). The accepted branch keeps a strong journal (`[ -z "$journal" ] || [ "$strong" = 1 ] || rm -f "$journal"`), but the conflict branch runs `[ -z "$journal" ] || rm -f "$journal"`.
- ps1 Send-MoeReceipt (scripts/moe-agent.ps1, about :2217). `$keep = $ok -and (Get-MoeProp $Report 'profile') -ceq 'verified-local'` is computed while $ok is still $false, so the conflict branch's `$ok = $true` deletes the journal.
Change exactly this:
- sh conflict branch: `[ -z "$journal" ] || [ "$strong" = 1 ] || rm -f "$journal"`, the accepted branch's own test. ($strong is the function's second parsed line: 1 when the report's own profile is verified-local.)
- ps1: `$keep = (Get-MoeProp $Report 'profile') -ceq 'verified-local'`, without the `$ok -and`. $keep is read only inside `if ($ok)`, so a refused or unanswered receipt behaves exactly as today.
- Both header comments: a strong journal outlives an accepted or a conflicting receipt until its attempt is closed, and finalize_postflight / Complete-MoePostflight or the next replay drops it. Keep the Twin pointers.
Do not touch:
- the conflict WARN text;
- RECEIPT_ACKED=true / return $true on a conflict (a conflict never defers the finalize; SR-T3 pins it);
- the non-strong conflict path, which still deletes its journal at once;
- any caller: the shared landing, wt_land_published / Complete-MoeWorktreeLanding, receipt_replay / Invoke-MoeReceiptReplay;
- the CQ-V08b removal in finalize_postflight / Complete-MoePostflight.
Error handling: no new failure path. The removal stays best-effort, as on the accepted branch (rm -f; -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue). A kept journal is settled by the existing pre-flight replay, which re-sends the receipt, finalizes a still-finalizing attempt, and drops a strong journal only once that attempt is closed.
Edit in the task worktree with the Edit tool (a TOOL witness, never sed -i), and keep moe-agent.ps1 UTF-8 with its BOM. Then run `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh` and checkRefs[0]'s ParseFile on both engines, and rerun the step 2 frozen row on both engines: it must now pass.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Under the strong profile (a receipt journal whose own profile is verified-local), a DELIVERY_RECEIPT_CONFLICT answer to record_delivery_receipt no longer deletes the journal. The conflict is logged once and counts as acknowledged (RECEIPT_ACKED=true / $true, so the finalize is not deferred). The journal stays until its attempt is closed: by finalize_postflight / Complete-MoePostflight's CQ-V08b removal, or by the next pre-flight replay, which re-sends the receipt, finalizes a still-finalizing attempt and only then drops it. A lost finalize after a conflict (live landing or replay, shared or worktree mode) therefore leaves a journal for the next replay, instead of stranding the attempt in finalizing with nothing to replay. A non-strong (legacy) journal is still deleted on a conflict, as today.
acceptanceCriteria: receipt_send (sh) and Send-MoeReceipt (ps1) keep a verified-local journal on DELIVERY_RECEIPT_CONFLICT and still delete a non-strong one; the conflict WARN line, the acknowledged return and every caller are unchanged.

Worktree mode, live landing (SR-T5, postflight-vm-route.sh and .ps1): a receipt conflict with every finalize lost gives one conflict line, 3 landed finalize tries, phase finalizing, no deferral, one journal-kept WARN, and the strong journal on disk with its fields unchanged.
Worktree mode, next pre-flight (SR-T5-replay): the replay re-sends the identical receipt, finalizes landed once, closes the attempt and drops the journal; nothing is re-frozen or re-dispatched.

Shared mode (frozen mode reconcile-strong-conflict-finalize-lost, in postflight.sh and .ps1): the live landing keeps the journal under a conflict plus a lost finalize; a replay whose finalize is lost again keeps it (one 'still finalizing after its replayed receipt' line); a replay whose finalize is answered closes the attempt and drops it; no ref moves, and nothing is re-frozen or re-gated.
The legacy frozen receipt-conflict row and SR-T1..T4 pass unchanged.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Fix at the call sites (re-write the journal after receipt_send, or skip it for strong journals): rejected. Three callers (shared landing, worktree landing, replay) would each need it, and receipt_send / Send-MoeReceipt already own the keep decision for an accepted receipt.
- Make a conflict defer the finalize like a refusal (RECEIPT_ACKED left empty): rejected. A conflict means a receipt already records this candidate, so deferring would hold every claim of the task for a replay that can only get the same conflict, and SR-T3 pins that a conflict finalizes at once.
- Split into an sh task and a ps1 twin: rejected. The runtime change is one condition per wrapper; splitting doubles the ~10 min three-engine gate and the QA pass for each half, and the wrappers would behave differently between the two landings.
- Use the fixture's finalize-loss: rejected. finalizeReply closes the attempt before it drops the answer, so it cannot show the stranding; the new combined mode reuses finalize_attempt-null's ok(null), which applies nothing.
- Put the full postflight.sh / postflight.ps1 in the gate: refused by the 20-minute rail. MOE_FROZEN_TEST_ONLY runs the receipt and strong-reconcile frozen modes in 31-49 s per engine (timed on e6c06b00's scripts), and CI runs the full suites.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- receipt_send / Send-MoeReceipt are the single place where every landing path (the shared landing, wt_land_published / Complete-MoeWorktreeLanding, receipt_replay / Invoke-MoeReceiptReplay) decides whether a journal outlives its receipt. The fix there covers all six cases the description names (live landing or replay, shared or worktree).
- The replay's CQ-V08b keep guard (`[ -n "$strong" ] && [ "$phase" != closed ] && [ -e "$f" ]`, ps1 twin with Test-Path) and finalize_postflight's removal need no change: after the fix they see the journal they used to lose.
- vm-route rows: vmr_run wipes $PROJECT and then calls $VMR_SETUP, and sr_restore restores a cp -a snapshot for a replay row. $OUT holds only the current run's output, while .moe/evidence-rpcs.jsonl carries over from the snapshot, so a replay row's fin and rec include run 1's rows.
- The frozen suite's replay(argv) reuses the mode's env object (set env.FAKE_EVIDENCE_MODE before each call) and always sets FAKE_CLAIM_MODE=finalizing. log2 is run 1's log plus that replay's own output.
